transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

My wife says I’ve been acting all over the place at work and at home, like I can’t control what I’m doing or keep it appropriate to what’s going on. She and my son really pushed for me to come in and get evaluated because they think it's gotten to be too much.
Have these behavioral changes been happening constantly and getting worse over time, or do they come and go in distinct phases?

It has been a gradual slide that's gotten progressively worse rather than coming and going. It started about a year ago when they introduced a new scheduling and inventory system at my store. Over the last six months, it has become a constant struggle where I feel completely off the rails.
Before these changes started about a year ago, did you experience any head injuries, a stroke, or other medical conditions affecting your brain?
No, I've never had any head injuries, strokes, or other medical issues with my brain before all this started. My health was always pretty solid up until this past year.
Along with these behavioral changes, have you or your family noticed any new difficulties with your memory, finding the right words, or planning daily tasks?

Yes, my family and I have definitely noticed those exact difficulties. When I try to explain simple things, I get easily derailed—like going off about barcodes turning into patterns—and I just can't seem to get back to the point. My wife and son also say they can't rely on me for daily planning anymore, like paying bills on time or following through on household plans, because I get too mixed up.
Have you or your family noticed any new changes in your eating habits, such as a strong craving for sweet foods, or any repetitive behaviors that you feel compelled to do?

I haven't noticed any changes in my eating habits or sweet cravings, but I definitely have those repetitive behaviors. I find myself pacing in tight circles, flapping my hands, or freezing in strange positions, and sometimes I'll repeat what others say under my breath. It really feels like I'm not in control of my body when it happens.
Have these difficulties with your memory, planning, and communication been getting steadily worse, and do they now prevent you from managing your everyday activities independently?

Yes, they have been getting steadily worse over the past year, especially during these last six months. It has definitely stopped me from managing things on my own, as I've been written up at work for chaotic shifts, and my wife and son have had to take over basic tasks like paying our bills.

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a one-year history of progressive behavioral and cognitive decline, characterized by early and prominent changes in personality, loss of social conduct/behavioral control, executive dysfunction (inability to plan, pay bills), and language difficulties (getting derailed, loss of focus). He also exhibits stereotypic/repetitive behaviors (pacing, hand-flapping, echolalia) and motor signs. These symptoms have caused significant functional impairment in his occupational and daily activities. The gradual, insidious onset and clinical presentation are highly characteristic of Frontotemporal Dementia (Dementia in Pick's disease, F02.0). Other causes like vascular dementia or head trauma have been ruled out.
